meta.description: A structured trading process, studied through data. Setup research, a learning path, and tools for analysing your own execution.

hero.lead: A defined process for reading liquidity, structure and execution — written down, tested against data, and taught step by step.
hero.sceneDescription: A scroll-driven diagram walking through one setup: market context, liquidity, sweep, market structure shift, fair value gap, then entry with a defined stop and target.

noise.label: Noise
noise.caption: Most of what you see is not a signal.

structure.label: Structure
structure.caption: Highs and lows start to describe intent.

liquidity.label: Liquidity
liquidity.caption: Resting orders pool where everyone agrees.

sweep.label: Sweep
sweep.caption: The level is taken. That is the point of it.

mss.label: Market structure shift
mss.caption: Direction changes, and it is measurable.

fvg.label: Fair value gap
fvg.caption: The imbalance left behind becomes the location.

entry.caption: Entry, stop and target defined before the trade.

system.label: System
system.caption: One repeatable process, not one lucky trade.

system.title: A setup is not the system
system.lead: A setup is one stage inside a closed process. What produces a result is the order of the stages, not an isolated pattern.
system.loopTitle: Data changes how the market is read
system.loopBody: The output of the last stage is the input to the first. That is what makes this a system rather than a checklist: review and data do not end the process, they decide what counts as context next time.

market.label: Market
market.question: What is actually in front of me?
market.body: The market produces movement all day. Most of it is information about positioning, not an opportunity. The first discipline is refusing to treat every move as a signal.

context.label: Context
context.question: Does this environment suit the setup at all?
context.body: Session, higher-timeframe direction, the range in force, the levels that matter. Context decides whether a setup is worth looking for, before any entry is considered.

liquidity.label: Liquidity
liquidity.question: Where are the resting orders?
liquidity.body: Price travels toward places where orders are parked. Equal highs and lows are obvious to everyone, which is exactly what makes them a destination rather than a barrier.

structure.label: Structure
structure.question: Has direction actually changed?
structure.body: A shift is a rule, not an impression. Structure gives the change a definition that can be checked afterwards, and disagreed with.

setup.label: Setup
setup.question: Does this match something written down?
setup.body: Context, liquidity and structure together produce a candidate, not a signal. A setup is a specification with conditions, and the Setup Lab is where it becomes a testable hypothesis.

execution.label: Execution
execution.question: What exactly triggers the decision?
execution.body: Entry, invalidation and target are defined before risk is taken. Entry is a decision point. It is not an outcome, and a trade that moved in your favour was not correct for that reason.

risk.label: Risk
risk.question: What is this allowed to cost?
risk.body: Invalidation is chosen from structure, and size follows from the invalidation. Risk is decided first because it is the only part of a trade fully under control.

review.label: Review
review.question: Was the process followed?
review.body: That question is separate from whether the trade won. A rule followed on a loser is a good trade; a rule broken on a winner is the expensive one.

data.label: Data
data.question: What do the records say?
data.body: Individual trades are anecdotes. Enough of them, recorded the same way, and the process starts describing its own behaviour, which is the only honest basis for changing it.

market.definition: The continuous stream of price and participation, before any interpretation is applied to it.

context.definition: The conditions surrounding a possible trade: session, higher-timeframe direction, range and volatility.

liquidity.definition: Areas where resting orders accumulate, which price tends to move toward rather than away from.

structure.definition: The sequence of swing highs and lows that describes direction in a way that can be checked.

setup.definition: A written specification of conditions that together identify a candidate trade.

execution.definition: Opening a defined position once its trigger conditions are met.

risk.definition: The predetermined amount a trade is allowed to cost, decided before entry.

review.definition: Assessment of whether the process was followed, kept separate from whether the trade profited.

data.definition: Accumulated trade records treated as a sample, used to describe the process rather than to justify it.

equalHighs.definition: Two or more highs at effectively the same price, marking a pool of resting orders above them.

equalLows.definition: Two or more lows at effectively the same price, marking a pool of resting orders below them.

sweep.definition: Price trading through a liquidity level and rejecting, taking the orders resting there.

bos.definition: Price closing beyond a prior swing point in the direction of the existing trend.

mss.definition: A break of structure against the prevailing direction, defining a change rather than a continuation.

displacement.definition: An impulsive move that leaves imbalance behind, separating intent from ordinary movement.

fvg.definition: The unfilled price range left behind by an impulsive move, often used as a location to act from.

entry.definition: The specific price and condition at which a position is opened.

invalidation.definition: The price at which the reason for the trade no longer holds.

positionSize.definition: The quantity chosen so that reaching invalidation costs the predetermined amount.

lab.title: A library of written hypotheses
lab.lead: Each setup is a specification: the conditions that have to hold, and the point at which it is wrong. None of them carry performance figures, because none of them have been tested yet.

liquidity-sweep-reversal.title: Liquidity sweep reversal
liquidity-sweep-reversal.purpose: A level everyone can see is taken, and the move that follows breaks structure in the opposite direction.
liquidity-sweep-reversal.context: A market that has been trending into an obvious high or low, with enough session time left for a reaction to develop.
liquidity-sweep-reversal.liquidity: A clear pool: equal highs, a prior session high, or a swing everybody is watching. The more obvious it is, the better it works as a destination.
liquidity-sweep-reversal.structure: Prior swing structure must be intact before the sweep, so the break afterwards is measurable rather than a matter of opinion.
liquidity-sweep-reversal.trigger: Price trades through the level and closes back inside, then displaces through the opposing swing point. Both halves are required.
liquidity-sweep-reversal.entry: The imbalance left by the displacement, entered on the retracement into it rather than chased at the break.
liquidity-sweep-reversal.invalidation: Above the sweep high, or below the sweep low. If price reclaims the level the reading was wrong, and nothing about it needs reinterpreting.
liquidity-sweep-reversal.risk: Sized so that reaching invalidation costs the predetermined amount. The distance is defined by the sweep, never by a preferred position size.
liquidity-sweep-reversal.review: Was the level genuinely obvious beforehand, or obvious only afterwards? That question separates this setup from hindsight.

session-open-displacement.title: Session open displacement
session-open-displacement.purpose: The first decisive move after a session opens, taken at the imbalance it leaves behind.
session-open-displacement.context: The opening window of a session with real participation. Outside that window the same pattern has a different meaning.
session-open-displacement.liquidity: Liquidity built during the quiet period before the open, in the range that formed while nothing was trading.
session-open-displacement.structure: No structural read is required before the open. The displacement itself creates the structure this setup uses.
session-open-displacement.trigger: An impulsive move away from the pre-open range that leaves an unfilled gap. Movement without imbalance does not qualify.
session-open-displacement.entry: The gap, on the first return into it. If price does not return there is no trade, and waiting is the setup working correctly.
session-open-displacement.invalidation: The far side of the gap. A fill means the imbalance is resolved and the reason for the location is gone.
session-open-displacement.risk: Tighter than most setups because the invalidation is close, which raises position size. Size still follows the stop, never the other way round.
session-open-displacement.review: Did the move actually displace, or was it a wide range bar in slow conditions? Recording that distinction is what makes the sample usable later.

equal-highs-draw.title: Equal highs as a draw
equal-highs-draw.purpose: Two highs at the same price are not resistance. They are a destination.
equal-highs-draw.context: A range or a slow trend where price has printed the same high more than once without breaking away.
equal-highs-draw.liquidity: The equal highs themselves. Orders rest above them, which is what gives price a reason to travel there.
equal-highs-draw.structure: Structure matters only as confirmation that the market is not already in a decisive move away from the level.
equal-highs-draw.trigger: Price beginning to move toward the level rather than away from it, in a session with enough time left to reach it.
equal-highs-draw.entry: Positional, into the draw. This is a directional bias rather than a precise trigger, and it is described that way on purpose.
equal-highs-draw.invalidation: A close beyond the opposite side of the range. At that point the equal highs are no longer the nearest draw.
equal-highs-draw.risk: Wider stop, smaller size. The trade-off is explicit: a positional idea cannot be given an intraday stop and still make sense.
equal-highs-draw.review: Did price reach the level at all? A setup that identifies a destination is judged on whether the destination was reached, not on the entry.

structure-shift-continuation.title: Structure shift continuation
structure-shift-continuation.purpose: A break in the direction of the existing trend, read as continuation rather than reversal.
structure-shift-continuation.context: An established trend with at least two confirmed swings in the same direction. Without that, the break has nothing to continue.
structure-shift-continuation.liquidity: Liquidity resting beneath the most recent higher low, or above the most recent lower high, in the pullback that precedes the break.
structure-shift-continuation.structure: The defining element. A break of structure in the trend direction, closed rather than wicked, measured against a swing that was there beforehand.
structure-shift-continuation.trigger: The close beyond the prior swing point, with the pullback that preceded it still intact.
structure-shift-continuation.entry: The retracement toward the broken level, which is now the nearest reference rather than a barrier.
structure-shift-continuation.invalidation: Beneath the low that produced the break. Losing it means the trend read is no longer supported by structure.
structure-shift-continuation.risk: Straightforward, because the invalidation is structural and does not need to be chosen. That is the argument for this setup over a discretionary entry.
structure-shift-continuation.review: Was the trend real at the point of entry, or two swings inside a range? Most losses on this setup are context failures, not trigger failures.

range-to-expansion.title: Range to expansion
range-to-expansion.purpose: A defined range, then the move that leaves it. The setup is the transition, not the range.
range-to-expansion.context: An extended balanced period, usually across a quiet session, with a range whose edges have been respected more than once.
range-to-expansion.liquidity: Both edges of the range hold liquidity. Which side is taken first is information, not noise.
range-to-expansion.structure: Inside the range, structure is meaningless. It becomes readable only once one side is left behind.
range-to-expansion.trigger: A decisive move out of the range that does not immediately return: displacement away from balance rather than another test of an edge.
range-to-expansion.entry: On the first retracement toward the range edge that was broken, treating it as the new reference.
range-to-expansion.invalidation: A return inside the range. If balance is restored the expansion did not happen and the premise is void.
range-to-expansion.risk: Position sizing is the hard part here. The stop is far by construction, so this setup is often correct and still unsuitable for the account.
range-to-expansion.review: How long was the range, and did that predict anything about the move? This is the setup where recording the context pays for itself.
